text.en: This Act may be cited as the Mining Act.

(1) In this Act and in any rules made thereunder"crude oil" means oil in its natural state before the same has been refined or otherwise treated but excluding water and foreign substances; "petroleum" includes any mineral oil or relative hydrocarbon and natural gas existing in its natural conditions in strata, but does not include coal or bituminous shales or other stratified deposits from which oil can be extracted by destructive distillation; "natural gas" means gas obtained from bore-holes and wells and consisting primarily of hydrocarbons; "minerals" means and includes coal, gold and all metals and substances in or under the ground by underground or by surface working, the ores of metals, and precious stones of all descriptions, but does not include crude oil, petroleum or natural gas; "to mine" and its cognate expressions includes all operations connected with the winning, smelting, or other treatment of minerals; "to prospect" and its cognate expressions includes all operations connected with the search for minerals but does not include search upon the surface of B.L.R.O. /11984 the ground not involving any disturbance of the soil below 3 feet in depth.

(2) It is hereby declared that the expressions "land" and "lands" in this Act include and shall be deemed always to have included the foreshores and the submarine areas the territorial waters of Brunei; and it is - further declared that the powers conferred on the Minister Act to issue or grant licences and leases thereunder be deemed always to have extended to such and submarine areas. No 3. Save as provided in the next succeeding subsection any person found to be prospecting or mining upon any land or mining or doing any act with a view to prospecting or mining on the same without having received lawful authority so to do any of the provisions of this Act, or in breach of any of the conditions thereof, shall be guilty of an offence: Penalty, a fine of $10,000, and all machinery, plant, tools, or other property together with any materials or products which may be found upon or proved to have been obtained from the land so unlawfully prospected or mined shall be liable to forfeiture.

LICENCES the provisions of this Act and any rules made thereunder His Majesty the Sultan and Yang DiPertuan in Council may from time to time issue licences to prospect for minerals.

(2) Such licences may cover lands alienated otherwise than for mining purposes either before or after the of this Act. Mode of 5. (1) Applications for such licences shall be in writing, name, residence and profession of the applicant, shall contain a description, sufficiently accurate for purposes of identification, of the situation, boundaries and area of the land over which the licence is required and shall specify the mineral or minerals for which the applicant desires to prospect.

(2) An index shall be kept in which all such applications shall be recorded serially in the order in which they are received and there shall be charged a fee of $500 in respect of every application so recorded:· Provided that the lodging or filing of an application shall or priority of claim as a matter of right to the issue of a prospecting licence and that it shall be lawful for His Majesty in Council, without assigning any cause, to refuse to issue any prospecting licence .. In the event of such refusal all entries in the index relating to such application shall be cancelled.

Notwithstanding anything herein contained it shall be lawful for the lessor by notice in writing from time to time to impose upon the lessee vary and rescind such restrictions and conditions as to the lessor shall appear necessary or desirable for the purpose of securing an adequate supply of fuel for the ships of the armed forces of Brunei or for other purposes of the armed forces of Brunei.

The lessee shall on notice from the lessor strengthen and support to the satisfaction of the lessor any part or parts of the mine when in the of the lessor such strengthening and support is needed for the of any road railway reservoir canal or other public work or any whether the said road reservoir canal or other public work or building shall be existing during the working of such part or parts of the mine already existing or shall be constructed after the said part or of the mine have been worked out. Such strengthening and support shall be made and done at the expense of the lessee if they are for the safety of any road railway reservoir canal or other public work or other buildiiJ,gs as aforesaid already existing at the time of the said part or parts of the mine by reason of the lessee having conducted mining operations within the limits prohibited by Clause 3 of Part III of and in other cases at the expense of the lessor.

A prospecting licence shall be issued for such a term Terms and as may be described by His Majesty in Council in each conditions particular case, and His Majesty in Council shall have power to extend such term upon such conditions as he may think fit is satisfied that the licencee has been prevented from completing his search of the land by any cause other than his own default.

(1) No prospecting licence shall be issued until the security applicant has deposited as security in respect thereof such sum, not being less than $100,000, as the Minister may de--

(2) In lieu of a deposit the Minister may accept from the applicant a bond with a surety approved by the Minister.
Every prospecting licence shall be substantially in the Forms form set out in Form I of the Schedule to this Act. B.L.R.O. l/1984

On or before the determination of his licence by Right of of time the licensee shall have a right, subject to licensee to lease the provisions of this Act, to a mining lease in accordance with the terms contained in any rules for the time being in force for mining leases.

heading.en: of alienated land required for mining

text.en: Except with the sanction of His Majesty in Council no Resumption mining title shall be issued for land which has been alienated of alienated under the Land Code (Cap. 40), but all land so alienated for mining shall be liable to be resumed for minin,g purposes by His purposes Majesty in Council upon payment to the grantee or other person entitled thereto of compensation for such interest in is conveyed by his title and for the improvements, if any, thereon; such compensation in case of disagreement shall be assessed in the manner provided by section 10 of the Land Code.

Subject to the provisions of this Act and any rules Power to made thereunder His Majesty in Council may, if the appli-issue mining cant is entitled to a lease under section 11 or if he considers that the applicant should be granted a mining lease, grant a mining lease in accordance with this Act.

(1) Every application for a mining lease shall be in Mode of writing, shall state the name, residence and profession of application the applicant, the name of the mineral for which the applicant intends to mine, and an address at which notices served shall be deemed to be duly served for the purposes of this Act. -(2) Every such application shall also be accompanied or sketch showing the area over which the proposed lease is to extend. heading.en: Condition implied to carry on mining operations

text.en: The lessee shall (save in respect of any working as to which the To deliver up Minister shall have sanctioned abandonment) at the end or sooner de-mines, etc., of the said term deliver up to the lessor in good order repair in good order and condition and fit for future working all mines which have been or may be made or sunk by the lessee under the licence and liberty in that behalf hereinbefore contained together with all engines pits shafts watercourses air-gates levels and fixtures below ground level and which cannot be moved without causing injury to the air mines except any pits or other works which shall have been abandoned or disused in the ordinary and fair course of working of the said mines and premises. B.L.R.O. 111984 THE LESSOR'S COVENANTS For quiet 1. The lessee paying the rents hereby reserved and observing and performing the covenants and provisions herein contained and on his part to be observed and performed shall and may peaceably and quietly hold and enjoy the rights and premises hereby demised for and during the term hereby granted without any lawful interruption from or by the lessor or any person rightfully claiming from or under him.

Every mining. lease shall by virtue of this Act and in of the absence of any express provision to the contrary, be subject to the following implied condition in respect of the land comprised therein, that is to say, that in case of a of or default of observance of any of the conditions of the said lease, whether expressed or implied by the proviof this Act, the Minister or any officer authorised by on behalf of His Majesty re-enter on the land comprised in such lease, or on any portion thereof in the name of the whole, and thereupon the same shall be forfeited to and vest in His Majesty: Provided that no re-entry shall be made on the ground of or default as aforesaid that may be capable of being repaired or made good, until after notice shall have been given to repair and make good such breach or default within such reasonable time as may be limited in the notice and the lessee shall nevertheless have persisted in his neglect or refusal to repair and make good the same: And provided further that forfeiture may be enforced notwithstanding the fact that rent may have been received such lease after the accrual of the liability to forfeiture, but so that if the forfeiture be enforced any rent received after the accrual of such liability shall be repaid.

It shall be lawful for His Majesty in Council to fix a Premium to be charged on lands alienated under mining that no premium shall be charged unless the of such premium shall have been made a special of the prospecting licence.

(1) The rents reserved on and the royalties to be paid Rents and of minerals won and removed from the lands royalties covered by a mining lease shall be such as His Majesty in Council may direct and shall be specified in the lease.

(2) The said rents and royalties shall be payable at the times and in the manner prescribed in such leases, without demand, and in the event of default being made in of such payments (of which default a notice in writthe Minister and served on the lessee shall be proof), the rents or royalties due shall be deemed to be an arrear and shall be recoverable in the manner prescribed by any law for the time being in force for the recovery of arrears of land rent.

Mining leases for coal shall be substantially in the Form of coal out in the First Schedule to this Act and may con-leases B.L.R.O. /1/984 12 CAP. 42 tain special conditions, where such seem desirable, in addition to any prescribed by the general provisions of this Act.

No mining lease for coal or other minerals shall be of transferable without the consent in writing, under the hand of the Minister first had and obtained. Form of 22. Mining leases for minerals other than coal shall be in of such form as the Minister may from time to time direct subject to the restrictions imposed by this Act.
